links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of qwen2.5:7b with versus without retrieval-augmented generation
links.effect: RAG raised qwen2.5:7b accuracy to 79.3% (χ²1=31.11, P<.001) with 85.9% retrieval precision.
links.quote: RAG implementation enhanced qwen2.5:7b's accuracy to 79.3% (χ²1=31.11, P<.001) with 85.9% retrieval precision.

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy difference between Chinese and English inputs
links.effect: Llama3.1:8b 67.8% English vs 31.4% Chinese (P<.001); Llama3.1:70b 90.1% vs 80.2% (P=.02); qwen2.5 models comparable across languages.
links.quote: Language effects varied across models: qwen2.5:7b showed comparable performance in Chinese (51.2%) and English (47.9%; χ²1=0.32, P=.57), whereas Llama3.1:8b exhibited significantly higher English accuracy (67.8% vs 31.4%; χ²1=40.20, P<.001).

unlisted_practices: Selecting LLMs by language relevance and parameter size for local deployment
Chain-of-thought reasoning distilled small model evaluation (Deepseek-R1:7b performed poorly)

screen.reason: The study tests whether adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to an open-source model improves its rare disease diagnostic accuracy compared to the baseline model.
